summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 55) in which a couple, Trish and her date, drive from San Luis Obispo toward a cemetery for a tombstone unveiling that his mother is holding. His mother phoned with directions, which Trish garbled, so they stop to buy a map and worry they will be late. Their playful banter over his Fretting, the coastal scenery, and a flirtatious hand-on-thigh moment fills out the scene.
one_line: A couple drives along the California coast from San Luis Obispo to a cemetery tombstone unveiling, delayed by garbled directions and playful flirtation.
key_facts: The couple needs directions from San Luis Obispo to the cemetery for a tombstone unveiling.
The man's mother gives the directions by phone and Trish repeats them as left, then right, then left, then a slight left, then up the hill.
Trish says the mother gives terrible directions and they stop at the next exit to buy a map.
The man says they are going to be late, and Trish replies that they now have an excuse because the mother knows they are late.
The man is described as someone who tends to Fret, and Trish calls it his job to Fret.
Once on secondary roads, the highway full of stopped cars and crane-necked drivers gives way to waves, beach and palms.
Trish rolls down the window and watches surfers wiping out in the curl as the car heads toward the boneyard.
Trish asks whether a date is the right kind of outing for a cemetery, and the man says it is just an unveiling, not a burial.
The man jokes that he pictures his mother cutting a ribbon with giant gold scissors.
The man slips a hand through the vent in Trish's apron-trousers and over her thigh, and she responds with Achtung!
Trish comments that the couple has only had eight dates, 20-some phone calls and about 100 emails.
Trish squeezes the man's hand tight enough to make his knuckles grind together while he is distracted by surfers on the roadside.
